# Final platform matrix (new18 §105)

Every tracked surface, all fourteen §105 columns, derived from the SSOT at release 1.9.1.
Facts checked at **2026-08-19** (the SSOT's own `generatedAt`; see §104 matrix for per-claim provenance).

**18 hosts** — 2 DEFERRED, 3 DISCOVERY_ONLY, 13 NATIVE.

This matrix reflects CURRENT reality, not the state assumed by the prompt that asked for it.
Two consequences of that are visible below and are not defects: most `mcp-stdio` primitives are
`AUDIT_REQUIRED` rather than `AVAILABLE` (a host documenting stdio MCP is not the same fact as
that host consuming the Official MCP Registry), and every `DEFERRED` / `DISCOVERY_ONLY` host
carries **no** truthful command — an advertised `--agent` form for one of them would be a lie
the harness gate reds on.

Audited 2026-08-27. Qwen Code publishes no gallery or catalogue of its own; it installs FROM other hosts' shelves and converts on the way in — `qwen extensions install <marketplace>:<plugin>` reads a Claude Code marketplace and converts the Claude manifest to `qwen-extension.json`, translating agents, skills and tool mappings, while `qwen extensions install <owner>/<repo>` does the same for a Gemini extension, carrying MCP servers and context files across. `/extensions explore` browses the Gemini CLI and Claude Code galleries. So this row is derivative of shelves we already publish or are working toward, and submitting to it is not a thing a person can do. Deliberately NOT marked available: no probe has installed CallLint through Qwen, so reachability is inferred from the documented conversion rather than observed, and ADR 0007 admits only observed acts as evidence. What would settle it is one command on a machine with Qwen Code — `qwen extensions install calllint/calllint` — after which this becomes an evidence-backed availability claim rather than a blocked row. Kept out of the to-do list because the to-do list is for acts a human can perform on a channel, and this channel accepts none. | https://calllint.com/harnesses/qwen-code | `agent-surfaces.json` | https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/<br>https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Code |
| OpenClaw | Open Source | mcp, skills, exec | NATIVE | `calllint scan --agent openclaw` | CallLint scans MCP configuration only. Skills and exec permissions are not covered. | yes | `openclaw-clawhub` | BLOCKED | channel: https://docs.openclaw.ai/clawhub | Blocked on a licence term, not on a missing channel — and the distinction is the point, because the mechanism here is real and one command long. Audited 2026-08-27. ClawHub hosts exactly three surfaces: Skills (a folder carrying `SKILL.md`), code plugins, and bundle plugins. It hosts no MCP servers, so the obvious reading of this row — publish the MCP server — has no target. But we already ship `skills/secure-agent-install/SKILL.md`, and `clawhub skill publish <path>` takes precisely that, with `--dry-run` first, so no new artifact would be needed. What stops it: publishing a skill to ClawHub releases it under `MIT-0`, and this repository is Apache-2.0. MIT-0 drops the attribution requirement and carries no patent grant, so the act would relicense a shipped artifact on strictly weaker terms than the repo it came from. That is an owner's decision about intellectual property, not an engineering step, and it cannot be inferred from the instruction to submit to shelves — so it is recorded here rather than performed. It also needs `clawhub login` (browser OAuth, `--device`, or a `clh_` token), which is an account only the owner has. DECIDED 2026-08-27: the owner declined, so this is settled rather than pending a decision. The alternative was checked before recording rather than assumed away, and it does not exist — ClawHub's skill format documents no `license` field and states in as many words that it `does not support per-skill license overrides`, with `All skills published on ClawHub are licensed under MIT-0`. So there is no way to list the skill on Apache-2.0 terms, and the channel is closed on a term we will not accept. Not a to-do and not a queue: nobody is reviewing anything, and re-running the audit will reach this same sentence. Two things that would reopen it, neither of which is work we can do: ClawHub adds a per-skill licence field, or it gains a surface that accepts what we actually ship. One route was deliberately left unexplored rather than silently dismissed — ClawHub also hosts code plugins, whose licence terms are documented separately from skills, but reaching it would mean building an OpenClaw plugin against their SDK with `openclaw.compat.pluginApi` and `openclaw.build.openclawVersion`, which is a new artifact and a new maintenance surface, not a submission. If that is ever wanted it should be decided on its own merits, not adopted as a workaround for a licence term. | https://calllint.com/harnesses/openclaw | `agent-surfaces.json` | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw |

## Column provenance

No cell above is typed. Each column is projected from a named SSOT field, so a claim here
cannot outlive the fact it describes:

| column | SSOT source |
| --- | --- |
| platform, vendor, support class | `displayName`, `vendor`, `supportClass` |
| authority surfaces | `authoritySurfaces` (closed 12-member enum) |
| exact current command | `truthfulCommands` — empty renders as an explicit "none" |
| coverage boundary | `coverageBoundary` (schema-required, so a host cannot ship without naming its limits) |
| Registry reuse? | whether any primitive carries `upstream: officialMcpRegistry` |
| native primitive, native state | the non-`mcp-stdio` primitives, else the stdio one alone |
| live/submission URL | `liveUrl` / `submissionUrl`; explicit `null` is rendered, not blanked |
| blocker | `primitive.blocker` |
| canonical human URL | `canonicalPath` |
| machine-readable presence | read back from the generated `agent-surfaces.json` cohort |
| watch source | `officialSources` — the same URLs `scripts/distribution-sources.json` gives the watcher |
